key_insight: Graph neural networks predict dissociative water adsorption on nickel using only bare-metal geometry, avoiding adsorbate construction and relaxation during screening.
engineering_relevance: The framework enables efficient screening of OH*+H* binding configurations on nickel nanoparticles containing up to approximately 3,000 atoms.
method: Define candidate O- and H-binding sites using sets of nickel anchor atoms.
Build adsorbate-free graphs from anchors and their local environment in MACE-relaxed bare nickel structures.
Use separate GNNs to predict DFT-reference adsorption energies and binding-site retention after relaxation.
evidence_signal: The energy model achieved 0.031 eV internal-validation MAE, with independent tests on unseen Ni55, Ni91, and Ni130 clusters and larger surface cells supporting transferability, particularly for relative-energy ranking.
watch_item: Quantitative accuracy varies across systems, so predictions on new nanoparticle geometries require validation.
paper_title: Adsorbate-Free Screening of Dissociative Water Adsorption on Nickel Nanoparticles via Graph Neural Networks
